brief.subject: Diesel jumps 9.7 cents; contract rate hikes hold above 10%
brief.headline: Diesel Climbs to $6.276 as Truckload Contract Rate Increases Stay Above 10%
brief.dek: Diesel rose 9.7 cents last week, contract rate gains hold above 10%, and CSX is pitching shippers on moving truckload freight to rail.
brief.lede: The U.S. average diesel price rose 9.7 cents to $6.276 per gallon for the week of 2026-10-19. That breaks a cooling trend and squeezes per-mile margins again.

sections.heading: Diesel Bounces Back Up
bullets: $6.276 per gallon is the U.S. average diesel price for the week of 2026-10-19, per EIA.
Up 9.7 cents (1.6%) week over week, so check that fuel surcharges are keeping pace on every load.
Still down 25.3 cents over four weeks, but last week's jump shows relief is not locked in.
Reefer operators burn fuel in both truck and trailer unit, so they feel each increase twice.

sections.heading: Contract Rate Gains Hold Steady
bullets: Above 10% is where truckload contract rate increases keep landing, according to a new SONAR index.
Carriers are winning in one cycle what would normally take several years of increases.
Small fleets renewing lanes now have leverage to push for higher contract rates.

sections.heading: CSX Courts Truckload Shippers
bullets: CSX is reviewing shippers' truckload files to offer service and cost comparisons for intermodal.
The railroad sees a chance to pull freight from a battered trucking market onto rail.
Long-haul dry van carriers should watch for shippers testing rail on longer lanes.

sections.heading: Rate Hikes and Cross-Border Moves
bullets: 5.9% general rate increase from Roadrunner takes effect Nov. 2, alongside a new Canada-to-U.S. LTL service.
5.9% average rate increase from UPS starts Dec. 21, matching FedEx's coming bump.
Oct. 30: plywood and certain packaging materials will no longer face the 50% Canada tariff, which could lift those flows.
$641M in U.S. trucking and warehousing activity comes from avocado imports out of Mexico.
